name: Improved Quadratic Taylor Inclusion Function
definition: An improved inclusion function that enforces constraints from both first-order (λ) and second-order (γ) Lipschitz constants. It behaves as a regular quadratic bound as long as its derivative is within $[-\\lambda, \\lambda]$, switching to a linear bound otherwise to prevent the quadratic term from growing too fast and providing loose bounds.
summary: The Improved Quadratic Taylor Inclusion Function computes tighter, valid bounds for sphere tracing by enforcing first-order Lipschitz constraints, preventing the quadratic derivative from growing too fast and ensuring larger, more efficient step sizes.
